### Feature orientation
Feature: Activity Event Backbone  [id: 1bc74e71-4587-45fb-94b7-4f830c7d8022]

Understanding: The daemon's live ObservedEvent stream and the DB schema's rawEvents/normalizedEvents were discovered to be completely separate pipelines with no connection, establishing the need for a unified event backbone. [s:2b589b44] The activity event table uses fully freeform categories, tags, and actor values — no enums, no taxonomy — with source_type/source_id back-references to originating records, and repo/branch/worktree as top-level columns; the embedding column is deferred as TEXT until pgvector is ready. [s:138200f0] Event emission follows the pattern of importing `emitEvents` and `ActivityEvent`, building events with freeform fields, and always wrapping in try/catch so failures never propagate to the parent operation; context fields (repo, branch, worktree) are auto-carried. [s:8e312af2]

Constraints:
  · Event categories, tags, and actor values are fully freeform — no enums, no conventions, no taxonomy document.
  · Events are self-contained and queryable without joins.
  · source_type/source_id back-references must point to originating records.
  · repo, branch, and worktree are top-level columns on every event.
  · Embedding column stays as TEXT until pgvector is explicitly added.
  · Event emission must always be wrapped in try/catch so it never fails the parent operation.
  · Timestamps must reflect actual session time, not digest time.
